app.title: CYRANO — Flow Cytometry Analysis Orchestrator
app.summary: A person uploads one raw instrument file to see what it holds: which plate well it came from, how many events it recorded, which detector channels it has and which signal types it measured. They can upload two files to set those same properties side by side in one table. Last, they upload all the files from a plate, and each file's event count is placed in its well on a 96-well plate heatmap, so empty or weak wells stand out across the plate.

task.text: Check what raw flow cytometry files contain, compare two of them, and see event counts across a 96-well plate at a glance.

data.text: Raw FCS files from a flow cytometer, one per well of a 96-well plate, with the well read from the file name and the event table read from the file.
data.item: an FCS file holding the events recorded from one well on a 96-well plate

stage.text: exploring and checking raw cytometer files right after acquisition, before gating and analysis

mechanism.text: Three tabs each take an upload: the first gives one file's properties as a table, the second sets two files' properties in parallel columns, and the third reads every file's well from its name and colours a plate-shaped grid of round wells by event count.

field.text: flow cytometry acquisition checks in cell biology

workflow.name: check what each data file holds and map one count across a plate layout

steps.here: each tab has its own FCS uploader: one file in Explore, two in Compare, many files from one plate in Analyze
a Property/Value table gives the well parsed from the file name, the number of events, the channel names and the signal types (Area, Height, Width)
two uploads side by side in two columns; once both are present, one table sets File 1 against File 2 for well, events, channels and signal types

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: every uploaded file whose name ends in a well ID (A1 to H12) is read, and its event count is stored under that well; files without a well ID are skipped

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: an 8×12 grid of round wells: empty wells are grey and filled wells are coloured on a yellow-to-red scale by event count, with a colour bar

distinctive: the plate position of each file is read from its file name by a naming rule ('..._A4.fcs'), not from the file's metadata
detector column names are split into a channel and a signal-type suffix (-A, -H, -W), so the summary lists channels and measured pulse features separately
the plate view follows the fixed 96-well layout with rows A–H and columns 1–12, and shows wells with no file as grey placeholders
the same summaries are available as command-line commands; the plate heatmap is saved as a PNG from the command line

parts.title: Explore / Compare / Analyze tabs
parts.summary: Splits the tool into three tabs: inspect one file, compare two files, or map a whole plate.

parts.title: Single-file summary
parts.summary: Takes one FCS upload and shows its well, event count, channels and signal types as a property table.

parts.title: Two-file comparison
parts.summary: Two side-by-side uploaders feed one table that sets each property of File 1 against File 2.

parts.title: Plate analysis
parts.summary: Takes all the FCS files from a plate, matches each to its well and collects the event counts that the plate heatmap draws.

parts.title: 96-well plate heatmap
parts.summary: Draws the plate as an 8×12 grid of round wells: empty wells are grey and the others are coloured by event count, with a colour bar.

parts.title: FCS file summarizer
parts.summary: Reads an FCS file's event table, counts its events, splits detector columns into channels and signal types, and reads the well from the file name.
